newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end up 0.01 pct in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end up 0.01 pct in listless trade.

text.p: Brazil shares seesawed to end virtually flat in cross-trading operations and with local players rolling over positions, brokers said.
"There's no fresh money coming in. Trading was listless," a senior trader said.
The Bovespa index of the 49-most-traded shares rose seven points to end up at 65,570 points. Turnover was moderate at 485 million reais ($471 million).
Traders welcomed last week's export figures, released today, of $845 million with a daily average of $211.3 million.
"We were expecting a lower average between $190 million and 195 million," another trader said.

Benchmark Telebras preferred shares ended up 0.46 percent at 76.90 reais. Power utility Eletrobras preferred shares rose 1.04 percent to close at 339 reais. Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred shares closed at 21.34 reais, up 1.62 percent.
Among big losers, oil monopoly Petrobras preferred shares dropped 1.11 percent to close at 134 reais.

Home appliances manufacturer Brasmotor preferred shares fell 6.42 percent to close at 277 reais on speculation that an increase in debt defaults expected for the end of the year could harm the firm's sales, brokers said.
